jpTimer._note: oneHourFrom of the super-hard weekends is a JP Saturday (the rows start on the JP Saturday since 06-11): 2018-05-05 = JP-SHR-95, the first 60-minute weekend (khux-guides digest of 5/4/2018 and reddit r/KHUx 8gzyzv «[5/5 ~ 5/6] ... only lasts 60 minutes», JP_ONLY.md Gap research 9; was 2018-05-12 until 06-11 round 4).

jpCensus._note: Corrections of the census JP rows from the JP research of 2026-11-05 and the live JP notice sweep of 2026-11-06 (user decisions 05-11 and 06-11), applied when the census is read (make-raid.js applyJpCensus); the private census file is not edited. Fields: make-raid.js applyJpCensus. Every probable choice has its label (jpBossProbable, jpHpProbable, jpRewardProbable) and is told in the Raid Bosses notice.

JP-RAID-21.source: JP notice 24013 (12/26/2016-1/1/2017; the census row starts on the Pacific day before): a daily rotating raid, a different boss every day, boss LV +10 per defeat; the bosses are not listed. The lineup is the worldwide «2016 Showdown!» (WW-E23794-1) of the same dates and rewards: probable.

costRuleNote: Raid AP and Bonus Time rule (raid-windows.js costRule; I-228). weekdayWeekend (user decision 06-11, served, not original): one rule for every raid quest, no exceptions (weekly, event, daily, Japan-only, kept): its original AP Monday to Friday (Pacific) with no Bonus Time, and 0 AP with Bonus Time all day (Lux x2, spawn gauge 6,000) on Saturday and Sunday; a tier whose original AP is 0 (a free week or an AP 0 campaign) costs weekdayZeroAp on weekdays (5: the usual paid raid quest price of 2017-2019, ours); raidWindows and bonusAllDay (June 2020) are off. originalWindows: the original opening hours of raidWindows with 90 AP outside them (06-11 «mixed», kept for a later return).

raidWindows._note: Used only with costRule originalWindows (off since the 06-11 weekday/weekend decision). Opening hours of the raids that had them (I-228, user decision 06-11 «mixed»; raid-windows.js, read by routes-raid.js and make-raid.js). Inside the hours: the raid's original rules (its census quest AP, the Lux and level rules of the time). Outside: open anyway (not original) at outsideAp per quest, no Bonus Time, a boss level of its own. Slots «HH:MM-HH:MM» with both minutes inside, on the real clock of tz (PT or JST); weekendSlots replace slots on Saturday and Sunday, weekendAllDay opens the whole weekend. levelReset «window»: the boss level belongs to one window (back to LV 1 at the next). A rule matches by censusIds, else by family / familyPrefix, jp and the entry's start in [from, to]; the first match wins. The 2018-01-08 Daily Raid Event (WW-E35529-1, notice 35529: «will appear all day») has no rule: all day, as the original.

rules.label: raidWindow
rules.source: Notices 29805, 31611, 33007 (2017-07, 09, 10): «Each day at the following times, the raid boss will appear for only one hour! 12:00 p.m. (PT), 7:00 p.m. (PT)». Proven.

rules.label: raidWindow
rules.source: Notice 33888 (2017-11-06): the same two one-hour windows; edited Nov. 10: Saturday 11 and Sunday 12 extended to 12:00-3:59 p.m. and 7:00-10:59 p.m. PT. Proven.

rules.label: raidWindow
rules.source: Notice 42150 (2018-07-09): four Raid Hours 2:00, 8:00, 14:00, 20:00 PT, one hour each. Proven.

rules.label: jpWindow
rules.source: JP notices 29893, 30969, 32002 and the JP wiki (2017-07 .. 2017-11): 12:00-12:29 / 22:00-22:29 JST, the boss level resets after each window. December 2017: same year, probable.

rules.label: jpWindow
rules.source: JP notices 41745 (2018-07) and 42600 (2018-08): 12:00-12:29 / 22:00-22:29 JST, «no level reset, the level carries over to the next window». January to June 2018: same year, probable.

rules.label: weeklyWindow
rules.source: Notices 44005 (2018-09-10) .. 54910 (2019-07-08): Monday to Friday the boss is available in the four listed hours, all day on Saturday and Sunday; 49544 (2019-02-01): 5 AP in those hours, 90 AP outside. Probable (players: unavailable outside the hours before 2019-02-01). Radiant Reward weeks (family «radiant reward») are not matched.

bonusAllDay._note: Used only with costRule originalWindows (off since the 06-11 weekday/weekend decision). Periods with Bonus Time 24 hours a day (raid-windows.js allDayBonus, routes-raid.js): the WW raids whose week starts inside a period are in Bonus Time at any hour (Lux x2, the AP 0 campaign). The original period starts at the weekly raid start, 2020-06-01 12:00 PT: here the week itself is the Shop week of the Story.

You can earn double the LUX from raid boss, and 0 AP Cost!»), 66114, 66617, 66626 («Bonus time will go on 24 hours all day until Jun. 30, 11:59 p.m. During bonus time it will be 0 AP cost and double the LUX!»). Proven.

reconstructedWhy.atk: No ATK of a raid is known after 2016. Story enemy ATK of the period, times the median boss/story ratio of the 23 weekly bosses with 2016 rows, times a tier share that has no source. Table and rule: raid_stats.json, docs/notes/raid.md.
reconstructedWhy.def: No DEF of a raid is known after 2016. 1000, or 1100 for rare 2: community calculators. Epic 50,000: a player report of no damage below about 50,000 STR, read as DEF without reading the damage formula; it may stop the deck that passed the Part 1 spike at about 1200 DEF. To change it, edit def in statsRule of raid_config.json and run node server/make-raid.js --stats, which copies it into raid_stats.json.
reconstructedWhy.hp: This boss, tier and week were not read on video: HP comes from the tier and period table. Before 2019-08-12 the shares below the cap at LV 30 are ours too (singleEra).
reconstructedWhy.hp_step: The week lies outside the dates this HP was seen in: change dates are known only between two video uploads, so the midpoint week decides, or the last value seen is carried on.
reconstructedWhy.atk_curve: Before 2019-08-12 stats grew with level. ATK below the cap follows singleEra.atkShare, which has no reading at all.
reconstructedWhy.moves: This boss has no 2016 row: it reuses the parts and moves of the row named in modelTemplates.
reconstructedWhy.attribute: The attribute of this boss is read from its colour (census: red Power, green Speed, blue Magic), not from a row: its template row has another attribute.
reconstructedWhy.background: The raid background of this map's world is incomplete (brokenBackgrounds): the fight draws the one of backgroundFallbackWorld.
reconstructedWhy.coinOdds: Coin amounts come from the wiki tables, often of the same tier in another week; the odds of the high amount and of gems have no source (rewards.reconstructed).
reconstructedWhy.rewards2016: Lux, Munny and EXP of the boss rows are the 2016 values of the template row (used only without the lux rule).
reconstructedWhy.lux: Lux of a defeat: the client sums luxAttack of the body and the broken parts at the boss's level, times the deck's Lux skills (bench). Original rule (official guide notice, Nov 2019): Lux follows the HP taken and the Lux skills, not hits or damage. Totals per kill reported with Lux++ on every medal, no bonus: Advanced about 8 billion, Legendary about 12 billion (forum), Epic about 19.8 billion (video frame, June 2021): 2% of body HP, divided by the x5 of our Lux++ skill (luxUp 50000, itself an estimate), spread as the template's luxAttack. Bonus time doubles it on the server. Munny and EXP stay the 2016 values.
reconstructedWhy.upMinutes: Weekly raids: about 20 minutes, timers seen in footage (19:39, 19:00, 17:00); 20:00 itself is not stated anywhere. Event raids of 2016-2018 with no 2016 setting of their boss: 10 minutes, 20 for a rare 2 body (eventUpMinutes).
reconstructedWhy.onlyCensusIds: Optional filter, absent in the shipped file (Task 8): only these census rows are built. Without it every WW row with week data is built, and raid-calendar.js picks the rows of the Shop week.
reconstructedWhy.eventUpMinutes: Timer of an event raid of 2016-2018 with no 2016 raidSetting of its boss: 10 minutes, 20 for a rare 2 body, as the 2016 story settings (Darkside 10 / Darkside Ω 20 ...).
reconstructedWhy.weekendUpMinutes: Weekend-only raids: 3 hours, 1 hour from the May 2018 weekend (reddit 8h8217, 2018-05-05: «counter 3 h to 1 h»). Applies to every weekend row without a 2016 setting dated on its own start.
reconstructedWhy.weekendTimer: Timer of a weekend-only raid from the weekend rule (3 hours, 1 hour from May 2018: one community post), not from a row of that weekend.
reconstructedWhy.setting2016: Timer and AP of a further attempt come from the boss's 2016 raidSetting of an earlier event (the only rows known), not from a row of this raid.
reconstructedWhy.eventCoins: The coin rewards of this event are not known: the one-tier level band table (LV 1-9, 10-19, 20-29, 30-99; wiki, 2018-09 on) of Raid Coins is used. Level drops named by the notices (Chips, Dales, event medals at LV 10, 90, 99 ...) are not served.
reconstructedWhy.eventHp_config: eventHp (user decision 4 Nov 2026, review I-1 option b): one-tier raids before capFrom with no video reading and no original row. Shape: the boss's own 2016 raidEnemy row (its template's when it has none), read at the knots. Scale: x1 on `from` (the last event of the 2016 tables), rising log-linearly by date to single.hp at single.level on single.date (RAID_VALUES.md: 1,000,000,000 at the LV 30 cap, Closehanded Captain, 2018-09-11), never below x1. The weekly one-tier rows of 2018-09 are flat above LV 30 («caps out at level 30»). Weekend raids before weekend.until: x factor («half of previous» on that weekend, reddit 8h8217). Three tiers of 2018: Beginner the line; Advanced LV 1 = advanced.lv1 (2018-07-23: «500,000,000 at LV 1», a week-long raid of three tiers, read as the hardest), with the boss's shape; Intermediate their geometric mean. The 1.2-16.5 billion cap of hp_tier_era applies from capFrom (2018-10-07) to 2019-08-11 only.
reconstructedWhy.eventHp: HP of an event raid of 2016-11 to 2018-08 (and of the one-tier weeks of 2018-09) with no original row: the boss's 2016 row scaled by date up to the 2018 readings (eventHp in raid_config.json). The readings are of unnamed bosses and tiers; the curve between them is ours.
reconstructedWhy.hpTier: The three tiers of 2018 have no HP reading of their own: Advanced takes the 2018-07-23 reading of 500 million at LV 1 (read as the hardest tier), Beginner the one-tier line, Intermediate the geometric mean of the two.
reconstructedWhy.levelDrops: Level drops named by the event's notice (Chip and Dale at LV 10, Setzer at 31 and 71, Young Kairi from LV 30, Halloween Sora at 90 ...): paid to the Present Box when the boss is defeated at that level. The rarity of a medal named without one is the only one the medal table has.
reconstructedWhy.levelDropsPartial: Some level rewards of this event's notice are not served: not itemised («bonus Medals»), a chance drop with no odds, a Boosted medal with no row, coins with no amount, or Event Coins every 5 levels with no amount.
reconstructedWhy.hpFloor: HP is never lowered: where the boss's own 2016 row is stronger than the one-tier rule at a level, that level keeps the 2016 HP.
reconstructedWhy.story: Story raid bosses (Task 11): tableLast = the last story quest of the 2016 stage table (thethiny 1.1.3 data, quests 1-555), whose stage.raidBoss names the original raidSetting of each quest; the master rows after it were copied by make-story-oltre.js with no source, so they are not read.
reconstructedWhy.storyBoss: The wiki gives «???» as this story quest's raid boss (89 quests between 614 and 825, HOLES.md): it takes the boss of the nearest quest with a known boss (the earlier one on a tie). Our choice, declared in the Notices.
reconstructedWhy.storyOmega: The Ω chance of this story quest is not known (outside the 2016 table, or its row names another boss): it uses the boss's rule below quest 555, the 2016 raidSetting the table gives that boss most often.
reconstructedWhy.storyConflict: The wiki and the 2016 table name different raid bosses for this quest (24 quests, HOLES.md): the census's choice (the wiki's boss) is used, as the plan rules; listed in the Notices.
reconstructedWhy.rareType2: The 2016 setting of this boss has rareUpType 2 (Guard Armor 3010, arg 6), a type whose meaning is not read: it is read as type 3, a chance of 1 in rareUpTypeArg.
reconstructedWhy.rareOdds: The rare boss of this quest (raidSetting rareBossId of the 2016 table) appears with a chance of 1 in rareUpTypeArg per spawn (rareUpType 3). The meaning of the two fields is inferred from their values (Fortress Crab 1: always the Ω the notice names; Queen Bee 5), not read.
reconstructedWhy.questObjectives: One objective of this event quest has no code here or pays an item we do not have (Avatar Coin, a keyblade or skill objective): the quest uses the standard Raid Time! objectives (Raid Coin x 5).
reconstructedWhy.boardStandard: No board of this raid is known: it gets the board of the nearest raid of the same type (spec, Answer 5), without the medals exclusive to that other event.
reconstructedWhy.boardGender: Both the male and the female board of this event are open: the original showed the one of the avatar's gender.
reconstructedWhy.weeklyUpMinutes: About 20 minutes: timers seen in footage (19:39, 19:00, 17:00); 20:00 itself is not stated anywhere.
reconstructedWhy.useAp: AP of a further attempt on the same boss: 10 in the 2016 rows, not stated for the Weekly era.
reconstructedWhy.tierQuestLv: Quest level per tier from the wiki pages. The Gem Drop Beginner page prints 125, taken as a slip.
reconstructedWhy.brokenBackgrounds: Incomplete raid backgrounds (docs/notes/raid.md, Backgrounds). A stage whose world has one uses backgroundFallbackWorld; the entry lists background in reconstructed.
reconstructedWhy.mapWorlds: Map name -> world when the story rows do not tell it. Otherwise the last story row with the same map, or with the same text before the colon. Fireplace: Beast's Castle (world 6), the world of the wiki quest pages that use the room (Lure a Submarine Carp, June 2017; Lure a Heartless Tsum).
reconstructedWhy.modelTemplates: Boss name -> 2016 raidEnemy id whose parts and moves it reuses, for bosses with no 2016 row; a boss not listed stays unavailable with why = template. Spiders 9101-9103 -> 5000 Enraged Arachnid: one rig for the three (identical frame, movie and place counts in all five fight animations), and 5000 is the 2016 recolour that already reused Savage Spider's moves. Egg Master 1008 -> 7 Trickmaster: identical frame counts in all five fight animations, 2 parts as in the JP raid_rule row. Inferred from the LWFs, medium-high confidence. The 15 reconstructed bosses (0018-0028, 0030-0032, 1011; render7/TEMPLATES15.md, coordinator ruling 2 Nov): a 2016 row whose part weaknesses equal the model's weak points, ties broken by equal frame counts, rare 1 preferred; no rig is shared, so moves, part HP shares and rarity are inferred (medium to medium-low confidence). The same rule for Jewel Sorceress -> 11 Savage Spider, Circus Crab -> 13 Fortress Crab and Crabby Cake -> 3 Behemoth (render9, user decision 4 Nov); Circus Crab shares Fortress Crab's frame counts in all five fight animations (medium-high confidence), the other two are medium and medium-low. Assault Dragon, Adventurer, Jewel Princess, Gear Golem and Closehanded Captain keep their full Default part set although later weekly weeks showed fewer parts on the wiki: every original LWF carries the full weak-point set, and an unpaired weak point crashes the client.
reconstructedWhy.modelParts: Boss name -> number of parts of its template row it keeps (the first ones). Spiders 9101-9103 -> 4 (coordinator ruling 2 Nov): the Spinneret (part 2 of 5000, weakness 2, 900 / 24,000 of body HP) and the 3 spiderlings (25% each), the 2016 to Jul 2018 layout. In the weekly raids (Sep 2018 on) only the Spinneret had a bar, but the only original spider LWFs with the Spinneret target (parts2) also mark the spiderlings as weak points (parts3-5), and a weak point without a part crashes the client (docs/notes/raid.md, Weak points). Declared in the Raid Bosses notice.
reconstructedWhy.bossAttributes: Boss name -> attribute (1 Power, 2 Speed, 3 Magic) for a boss on a template row whose own attribute differs; body and parts take it. The spiders' attributes come from their colour as the census reads it (inferred). The 15 reconstructed bosses: body attribute from the khuxwiki infobox where the template differs; their parts take it too, not the wiki's per-part attributes.
reconstructedWhy.singleEra: One tier before 2019-08-12: stats grow up to a cap at LV 30 (one forum statement). Cap HP is read from footage; the shares below it are ours, fitted to the only readings: LV 2 above 2%, LV 4 above 3%, LV 24 about 50%. atkShare has no reading at all: it follows the shape of the 2016 rows. Knots are the coin level bands.
reconstructedWhy.lux_config: lux: perHpFullDeck = Lux of a kill with Lux++ on every medal, as a share of body HP (fit: Advanced 400B -> 8B, Legendary 700B -> 12B, Epic 1T -> 19.8B); fullDeckMultiplier = the Lux multiplier of that deck in our skill table (Lux++ luxUp 50000). Row Lux at a level = body HP x perHpFullDeck / fullDeckMultiplier.
reconstructedWhy.statsRule: Inputs of raid_stats.json. refEnemyId: the plain Shadow row, the reference story enemy. def: community calculators treat raid DEF as constant at about 1000, 1100 for Omega; epic: a player report of a threshold near 50,000 STR, read as DEF. The damage formula was not read, so that reading is an assumption.
reconstructedWhy.partHp: Part HP: JP screenshots of 5 bosses as a share of the body where derived, the nearest date; otherwise the body-to-part ratio of the 2016 row at its first knot.
reconstructedWhy.boards: Raid Boards (raid-boards.js): unmatched lists reward names with no item in the master tables; their cells are left off the board and reported, never replaced by another item. aliases maps a wiki name to the item it means, with the reason; the week gets the label boardAlias. reconstructedTexture lists the rewards drawn with a reconstructed texture (label boardTexture). background = sphere.boardId of every Raid Board (img/sphere_board/Board_0005, the lilac card of the original screenshots). art gives each board key its card picture, served as img/sphere_incentive/<sphereBoardId>.png: jp = the JP 4.3.1 file with the same picture, matched pixel by pixel against the khuxwiki screenshots of the WW boards (reference/raid_boards); screenshot = no JP file has it, so the card is cut from that screenshot by recon/tools/raid_board_screens.py (label boardArt). A board with no art gets the label boardNoArt.
reconstructedWhy.boardArt: The card picture of one of this week's Raid Boards is cut from a screenshot of the original game: the picture file itself was not found.
reconstructedWhy.boardNoArt: One of this week's Raid Boards has no card picture: its original was not found.
reconstructedWhy.boardArtWiki: The card picture of one of this raid's Raid Boards is the original card as shown on the Japanese fan wiki (wikiwiki.jp/khux, page レイドボード; 179-359 px), scaled to 306 px: the picture file itself is not in the surviving Japanese game data (JP_ONLY.md Gap research 10).
reconstructedWhy.jpBoardProbable: The Raid Board is an original Japanese board of the shared 2017 master whose tie to this raid is probable, not proven: JP-RAID-3 (November 2015) = board 4400001, the only board of that month, with the title True (真・) unlocked by its Cid cells as the JP wiki says of the November 2015 raid board.
reconstructedWhy.boardPath: The positions of the cells on the Raid Boards are ours: the cells follow one path from START in the wiki's order n (the original layouts, visible in the khuxwiki screenshots, are not restored yet). Whether cells had to be bought in order is not documented.
reconstructedWhy.boardSet: Which boards ran this week is inferred: the board names are sourced, the layout of that week is not (2021-03-01 to 2021-06-29 and the one-day event of 2020-11-01).
reconstructedWhy.boardCost: A board cost corrected from the wiki: Halloween Board 2019, cell 17 reads 700 on the wiki, but the page total and the cost ladder need 1,600 (inferred).
reconstructedWhy.boardCells: Some cells of this week's boards are missing: their reward has no item here, so the cell is left off rather than replaced.
reconstructedWhy.boardTexture: A Spirit part of this week's boards (Starlight Ears, Dazzling Disco) is drawn with one reconstructed texture: the original is lost (a small sparkle, a tiny dot).
reconstructedWhy.boardAlias: A board reward named differently on the wiki is matched to another item: 6★ Fantasia Mickey A is given as the 5★ Fantasia Mickey A (no 6★ exists).
reconstructedWhy.jp: Japan-only raid (census JP row, I-232): served only in the Raid Catalog, never as a raid of the week (spec Answer 3); one tier, its boss, dates and HP from the JP sources (wikiwiki.jp, khux-guides digests of the JP notices).
reconstructedWhy.jpQuest: No JP quest page survives: the quest plays on the map file of the WW event raid of the same boss nearest in date (else the nearest WW event raid), with its level, AP and world, and the standard Raid Time! objectives (make-raid.js jpDonorOf).
reconstructedWhy.jpDates: The JP source gives only the start date: the raid is dated one week from it.
reconstructedWhy.jp2016: HP, ATK, DEF, Lux and rewards are the boss's 2016 worldwide row as it stands (census «yes (2016 row)»): the JP values of this run are not known and may differ (the JP wiki notes it for Hocus Pocus 2015 against 2016).
reconstructedWhy.jpTimer: Time limits of the JP wiki: super-hard weekend raids 12 hours, 1 hour from the 2018-05-05 weekend; the monthly «30-minute» raids 30 minutes (their two daily windows, 12:00 and 22:00 JST, are raidWindows: label jpWindow).
reconstructedWhy.weekRule: I-228 (user decision 06-11, not original, one rule for every raid, worldwide and Japanese alike): the raid quest costs its original AP from Monday to Friday (Pacific time) with no Bonus Time at any hour, and 0 AP with Bonus Time all day (Lux x2, spawn gauge 6,000, the Bonus Time level steps) on Saturday and Sunday, for every raid. The originals had their own hours instead: four one-hour Bonus Times a day (0 AP or halved AP, Lux x2), daily raids open only in their windows, weekday weekly raids of 2018-09 .. 2019-07 only in the Bonus Time hours (raid_config.json raidWindows, costRule originalWindows).
reconstructedWhy.weekdayAp: I-228 (user decision 06-11, no exceptions): the original AP of this quest is 0 (a free week, or an AP 0 campaign of the time); under the weekday/weekend rule it costs weekdayZeroAp (5 AP, the usual paid raid quest price of 2017-2019, ours) from Monday to Friday and 0 on Saturday and Sunday.
reconstructedWhy.raidWindow: I-228 (user decision 06-11, mixed): the WW Daily Raid Event boss appeared only in its windows (notices 29805, 31611, 33007, 33888: 12:00 and 19:00 PT, one hour; 33888 edited Nov. 10: 12:00-15:59 and 19:00-22:59 PT on Saturday and Sunday; 42150: the four Raid Hours 2:00, 8:00, 14:00, 20:00 PT). Inside them the quest costs its census AP and the Lux and level rules of the time apply. Outside them the raid stays open (not original) at raidWindows.outsideAp (90 AP per quest, the price of the weekly raids outside their hours from 2019-02-01, notice 49544), with no Bonus Time and a boss level of its own; the master stage useAp is that 90 (shown on the quest top), so inside a window the quest top shows 90 and charges less, unless the AP 0 campaign shows 0.
reconstructedWhy.jpWindow: I-228 (user decision 06-11, mixed): the JP monthly 30-minute raids opened 12:00-12:29 and 22:00-22:29 JST (JP notices 29893, 30969, 32002, 41745, 42600). In 2017 the boss level went back to LV 1 after each window (proven July to November 2017; December 2017 follows its year: probable); in 2018 it carried over to the next window (JP notices 41745, 42600, July and August 2018; January to June 2018 follow their year: probable). Outside the windows the raid stays open (not original) at 90 AP per quest, with no Bonus Time and a boss level of its own that never touches the window level (its usual rule: +1 per defeat, LV 1 on the 1st of the month). The boss of the day still follows the Pacific weekday (July to September 2017).
reconstructedWhy.weeklyWindow: I-228 (user decision 06-11, mixed; probable): from 2018-09-10 (notice 44005) to the week of 2019-07-08 (54910) the weekly raid boss was available Monday to Friday only in the four Bonus Time hours (2:00, 8:00, 14:00, 20:00 PT) and all day on Saturday and Sunday. Before 2019-02-01 players report it unavailable outside those hours (reddit 2018-09 .. 2019-01, screenshot of 2018-09-11); from 2019-02-01 (49544) the quest cost 5 AP in those hours and 90 AP outside. Here every such week is open outside the hours at 90 AP, with no Bonus Time and a boss level of its own (probable for 2019-02 .. 07, not original before); inside them it costs its census AP (5 from 2019-02-01). Radiant Reward weeks are left all day (a player report: gem weeks open 24/7).
reconstructedWhy.jpBoardDeduced: Reconstructed Raid Board (user decision 06-11): no JP board of this raid survives cell by cell, so it is built from what the evidence says (the JP wiki board summary: cell count, total Raid Coins, main rewards, title; the JP board card pictures of the 4.3.1 client; the KH2.8 boards read from a video), on the model of the original JP boards of the same period (cost curve of the Christmas 2015 / January 2016 boards or of the KH2.8 sets, scaled to the stated total), with the JP rewards mapped to worldwide items (titles: the worldwide title rows in JP order, probable). Cell positions, the costs of single cells and the filler medals are ours.
reconstructedWhy.jpBoardOriginal: Original Raid Boards: the Japanese board rows of this raid (cells, costs, rewards, completion) survive in the shared 2017 master; JP-only medals with no worldwide item are left off (boardCells), and a JP medal with a worldwide twin is that twin (Mickey & Magic Broom = Fantasia Mickey B, Sora Santa Ver. 5★ = Christmas Sora 5★). The cell positions are ours.
reconstructedWhy.jpNoBoard: No Raid Board: nothing is known of this raid's Japanese board (or the JP wiki gives neither its cell count nor its total), so none is served (user decision 06-11). The raid still pays Raid Coins.
reconstructedWhy.jpBoard: The JP super-hard weekend board (JP wiki: 13 cells, 40,500 Raid Coins, 6★ Moogle x3, Huey & Dewey & Louie x8, Magic Broom x2, completion 6★ Moogle) is the WW Legendary Raid Reward board of WW-E41605-1, which has the same cells, items and total cost (jpBoards.superHard).
reconstructedWhy.jpQuestAp: Quest AP of a JP row when the JP wiki states it (November 2017 monthly raid: AP 0).
reconstructedWhy.jpCensus: Corrections of the census JP rows from the later JP research (bosses by weekday of the 2017 monthly raids, the year-end 2016 daily raid, the two 2018 weekends, the JP level drops; from the live notice sweep of 2026-11-06 the notices' JP dates, 3-hour time limits and level steps), applied when the census is read; the census file itself is not edited.
reconstructedWhy.jpBossProbable: No JP source names this boss directly: it is inferred (jpCensus). Year-end 2016: the worldwide «2016 Showdown!» lineup of the same dates and rewards. September 2017 Saturday: «Furious Whole Cake» read as Crabby Cake. (The weekends of 2018-08-04 and 2018-09-01 are named by their own notices since 2026-11-06: no longer probable.)
reconstructedWhy.jpHpProbable: No HP source for this weekend: the players' reading of the 2018-06-23 weekend raid (about 1.5 billion, fixed at every level) is carried over.
reconstructedWhy.jpRewardProbable: A level drop of the JP notice is given as the worldwide medal it most probably was (rarity, bonus or guarantee not stated): Mickey & Minnie 6★ (Valentine 2016, LV 95), Prince & Belle 6★ (White Day 2016, LV 95), the boosted Trickmaster 6★ +1,000 STR (July 2017, Saturday LV 10).

6★ Fantasia Mickey A.why: Fantasia Mickey A exists only at 5★ (Roboloid's full medal list, the medal table); the board pairs it with Magic Brooms, the 5★ evolve recipe, and the wiki infobox lists it as mickeya=1 without a rarity: the 6★ is read as a slip of the wiki layout.

reconstructed.coinType: Reward type of the Raid Coin: the 2016 rows pay the Weekly-era bosses (13, 14, 1003, 1004, 1009) in type 16 and event bosses in type 15 Event Coin. grantItem pays both 15 and 16 into raidSpherePoint so no original row loses its reward. The icon is checked on the bench.
reconstructed.oddsBase: Odds read as base 10000, rolled from the last slot to the first, slot 1 taking the rest (the 2016 rows then give round shares: 1/3 each, 92/8, 70/30). Inferred from the numbers, not from code.
reconstructed.oddsUpFromLevel: oddsUpPerLv is added to the chance of every slot after the first for each level above this one. The field is undocumented (name only), so this is a guess; every coin row built here has oddsUpPerLv 0, so coins are unaffected.
reconstructed.highCoinPct: Chance of the higher Victory coin amount: a player counted about 5,200 coins over LV 1-29, which fits about 10% high rolls; no source gives the odds. Matches the 92/8 pattern of the 2016 two-slot rows.
reconstructed.gemPctByTier: Total chance that a Gem Drop table pays a gem (split evenly over Magic, Speed, Power) instead of coins. Only the rule is official (notice of 2020-03-16: every reward type has a chance of a gem, higher with the difficulty); the numbers are invented to rise by tier.
reconstructed.gemMaterialIds: Material ids of the gems as used elsewhere in this server (make-proud.js, make-moogleshop.js).
reconstructed.bandsBefore: Amounts by level band for the single tier, 2018-09 to 2019-08-11: wiki tables, one table per period in all direct rows.
reconstructed.tiers: Amounts by tier from 2019-08-12 (LV 1-99 flat): wiki tables, 86 direct rows with no exception; Legendary and Epic rest on one direct row each.
reconstructed.tierFrom: Date the tiers replace the level bands (notice of 2019-08-12).
reconstructed.gemOnlyLow: In Gem Drop tables the Victory slot offers the low coin amount or a gem; the wiki prints no high amount there (could be an editor's simplification).
